create.name: Three Treasures Sangha
create.bio:
Three Treasures Sangha is a lay Zen community in Seattle and one of the groups affiliated with the Diamond Sangha, the lineage that Robert Aitken Rōshi brought from the Sanbō Kyōdan school to Hawaii. The group has met for more than twenty-five years. Aitken himself was among its early teachers, followed by Jack Duffy Rōshi, an Aitken heir who led it until he stepped back at the end of 2021. Its present teacher is Lee Shields, who received independent teaching status in a transmission ceremony that November, with Madelon Yamane Bolling also teaching. Practice combines silent sitting, sutra chanting, talks and private interviews, and students may work with breath-counting, koans or just sitting.

The sangha's home is Dharma Gate, a renovated house in south Seattle with a zendo, an interview room, a library and a garden for walking meditation, which it shares with a mindfulness community. Sittings run on Wednesday evenings in person and on Zoom, with early-morning Zoom sittings on weekdays. A one-day zazenkai is held most months, and two seven-day sesshin a year alternate between a residential retreat at a camp in western Washington and a non-residential one in the city. Newcomers are asked to attend an orientation first, and transcripts of recent talks are posted on its website.

courses.title: Residential Sesshin with Jack Duffy and Lee Shields, March 2027
courses.description: A traditional seven-day silent retreat at Samish Island Camp and Retreat Center in western Washington, led by Jack Duffy Rōshi and Lee Shields, with long days of sitting and walking meditation, daily dharma talks and private interviews. Those new to sesshin are invited to get in touch first.

courses.title: Zazenkai (monthly day of practice)
courses.description: A one-day sitting retreat held most months at Dharma Gate and on Zoom, led in turn by the sangha's teachers, with zazen, walking meditation and a talk. Longer two-day intensives and the twice-yearly sesshin are listed on the same calendar.

courses.title: Orientation for newcomers
courses.description: Beginners, and Zen students new to the group, are asked to attend an orientation before sitting with the sangha. It covers the forms of the lineage and answers questions; it is arranged by phone.

courses.title: Membership
courses.description: Regular members commit to a sitting practice and help run the sangha; supporting members take part less often. Both receive the member rate for sesshin, and weekly sitting stays free for everyone whether or not they join.
courses.price: dues of $35/month, though membership is not contingent on ability to pay

free_resources.title: Zen talks
free_resources.description: Transcripts of dharma talks given at the sangha's zenkai and sesshin, mostly by Lee Shields with some by Madelon Bolling, posted shortly after they are given and often working through a koan or a classic Zen text.
